newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures extend losses late, end lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures extend losses late, end lower.

text.p: U.S. debt futures extended losses in late afternoon trading to end moderately lower but above session price troughs.

Selling picked up in earnest after the five-year Treasury note sale, although viewed as good, still failed to stir up enough buying to keep June U.S. Treasury bond futures above the 108-03/32 level, floor brokers said.
They also noted signs that hedge funds which had bought during Tuesday's afternoon rise may have bailed out as June T-bonds broke back down below the 107-28/32 level.
The five-year note sold at 6.745 percent compared to forecasts for 6.76 percent, with a bid/cover at 2.58 and non-competitive bids that totalled $667 million.
One broker also said that dealers who bought the five-year note may have sold out as the market began declining.
"It appears they may have bought the five-year a little bit too expensive," said one floor broker.

They said remarks by Atlanta Federal Reserve president Jack Guynn may have added to the downdraft that already was in progress. He said he sees continued moderate growth in 1997 but that the Fed must be preemptive regarding inflation.

Futures firmed early on optimism about a potential balanced budget pact. Senate Majority leader Trent Lott said during the afternoon that he hoped an announcement on budget talks could be made early next week.

Chartists warned against reading too much into Wednesday's fall that pushed June bonds back to the bottom of Tuesday's range. "I wouldn't overreact in an auction market," said one broker. "It's just kind of rehashing yesterday's range."
June bonds fell 13/32 to 107-23/32, notes off 8/32 at 105-26/32, munis down 11/32 at 112-30/32, Sept bills lost 0.025 to 94.305, Euros lost 0.025 to 93.735.
